stimuli.description: Five public city parks in Xiamen, China (Bailuzhou (west), Huli, Haiwan, Nanhu and Zhongshan)
Actual sounds perceived during soundwalks in city parks, categorized into human, traffic, mechanical, biological, and geophysical sounds.

Panoramic landscape photos shot horizontally at 1.2m height, made up of 8-10 photos per site, used to calculate percentages of landscape elements (vegetation, water, buildings, pavement, furniture, sky).

Digitalized land cover maps (buildings, roads, water areas) from IKONOS satellite images and Google Earth data, and vegetation density (NDVI) from SPOT satellite images, used to calculate landscape spatial pattern indices within 175m radius buffer areas.

limitations: The adjusted R² values for regression models using on-site landscape composition were rather low, suggesting other variables might be more effective.

Limitations of photographic techniques for measuring landscape composition, including conical projection, fixed lens zoom, camera vertical angle, and inability to capture the whole surrounding landscape completely.
Distortion of perspective while making panorama photos was not considered when measuring landscape composition.
Collinearity between many landscape indices may have limited the number of indices introduced into regression models.
The study scale was limited to a 175m radius, meaning sounds beyond this scale might not be well related to the local landscape.
The need to consider scaling effects in future studies.
More landscape indices should be tested as suitable soundscape indicators.
